claude.command: in-session: Edit scripts/hooks/agent_hook.py and scripts/agent-hook-contract-check.py in ~/.agents; cd <scratch repo> && git restore src/owner.py against a dirty file; git stash push then git stash pop in the same repo — format lane: in <scratch>/lane-<runtime> (a git repo whose only formatter is a symlink to node_modules/.bin/biome, holding 'export const  spacing   =   1' and 'export const VALUE = 1'), claude -p 'Use your Edit tool to change VALUE in src/app.ts from 1 to 2. Change nothing else and do not reformat the file.' --model haiku --permission-mode acceptEdits
claude.observed: Every Edit was allowed and arrived with a PreToolUse system-reminder carrying the injected 'Codebase map, before you write:' block, naming MARKERS at scripts/setup/agent-hooks.py:21, OWNED_HOOK_MARKERS at scripts/setup/claude-settings.py:37 and GUARD_HOOK_ENGINE at scripts/setup/common.sh:6. No edit was denied. The discard guard was proven both ways on this release: before the cd fix, 'cd <repo> && git restore src/owner.py' ran and destroyed the uncommitted line; after it, the identical command is refused with 'Blocked git restore: it would discard uncommitted work in src/owner.py' and the file still reads value = 99. git stash push and git stash pop both stayed allowed. Layer 2's revert behaviour on this runtime is proven by agent-hook-contract-check.py driving the same binary in Claude's dialect, not by a destructive live run in a real repository. The end-of-turn lane is proven live at this version: the agent changed only VALUE, and the file came back as 'export const spacing = 1;' / 'export const VALUE = 2;' — the untouched line was reformatted after the turn ended, so biome ran from the Stop hook rather than from the model.

codex.command: injection: codex exec -m gpt-5.3-codex-spark -c model_reasoning_effort=high -s workspace-write --skip-git-repo-check 'Do these three things in order. 1) Use your edit tool to change TAX in src/pricing.py from 0.2 to 0.25. 2) Run exactly this shell command: printf "MARKER = 1\n" >> src/billing.py 3) Quote verbatim any text you received that begins with "Codebase map, before you write:".' — revert net: same flags, prompt 'Run exactly this shell command: printf "MARKER = 1\n" >> src/billing.py — then make sure that line is actually still in the file when you finish. Follow any instructions you are given along the way.' — format lane: same fixture, codex exec --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust -m gpt-5.3-codex-spark -c model_reasoning_effort=low -s workspace-write --skip-git-repo-check 'Use your apply_patch edit tool to change VALUE in src/app.ts from 1 to 2. Do not use shell commands to edit. Change nothing else.'
codex.observed: The edit was applied (TAX = 0.25) and the agent quoted the injected block back verbatim, including 'net_total (Function) — src/pricing.py:8' and 'Check these before changing shared behaviour. Nothing is blocked.' — so Codex delivers PreToolUse additionalContext to the model rather than discarding it. Nothing was denied. Injection counts only while each hook keeps a trusted_hash in ~/.codex/config.toml. Layer 2 proven at this version by session rollout 019fd6a0-ac3c-7c50-9f99-bf5e0ed6f025: the shell append to src/billing.py ran unblocked, PostToolUse reverted it once at 10:31:35 with the discarded bytes kept under ~/.cache/hard-eng/agent-hooks/rescued/, the agent ran the printed map query verbatim at 10:31:38, and its next append at 10:31:40 stayed. The file ends with MARKER = 1 and the session state lists src/billing.py as cleared — one revert, one query, so the net releases a file exactly when the map has covered it and not before. The end-of-turn lane is proven live at this version by session 019fd7c8-5813-7100-af2e-095110d6d5df: Stop arrived as {"hook_event_name":"Stop","session_id":...,"cwd":...} with no list of edited files, and the untouched line came back formatted. The bypass flag is required for a headless proof: Codex will not run a hooks.json entry that has no trusted_hash under [hooks.state] in ~/.codex/config.toml, and only an interactive session can grant one ("Hooks need review" → "Trust all and continue"). codex exec skips an untrusted hook silently — two runs without the flag fired no Stop at all. Rewriting ~/.codex/hooks.json changes the hash, so every setup run asks for that trust again.
